steps.text: Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a frying pan over low heat; cook and stir onion in melted butter until lightly browned, 5 to 8 minutes.

Mix bread crumbs, water, and half-and-half in a large bowl; let stand for about 2 minutes. Stir cooked onion, ground beef, ground pork, salt, white pepper, and sugar into bread crumb mixture until thoroughly mixed. Shape mixture into about 48 very small meatballs.

Melt 3 tablespoons butter in a skillet; add meatballs. Brown slowly, allowing about 25 minutes, until meatballs are fully cooked in the middle and no longer pink. Shake pan occasionally to cook evenly.

raw_recipe.headline: Swedish Meatballs (From a Swede!)
raw_recipe.description: These tiny Swedish meatballs use a combination of ground beef and ground pork to make a flavorful appetizer for holidays or dinner parties. Serve alongside vegetable sour cream or lingonberry sauce for an authentic Swedish meal.
raw_recipe.name: Swedish Meatballs (From a Swede!)

review.reviewBody: Very good. We added about 1/4 c finely shredded hard cheese. I would also suggest dusting your hands with flour to keep them from sticking to you. The flavor was very nice, make sure to cook them slow but not too slow because they will burn.

AKA “fly off the table” Swedish Meatballs
I made a double recipe of these meatballs as is. That being said, they can be changed slightly at no taste cost if you are on a ketogenic diet: substitute bread crumbs for flax meal, half-and-half for heavy whipping cream and a pinch of stevia for the sugar. Now back to the actual recipe. I made these little puppies for New Year’s Eve. My mother told me: “Wow, I haven’t had any of these in so long! I used to make these all the time.” Outcome? My sister-in-law did not even get to eat one! These morsels just disappeared in less than ten minutes. I am not kidding. I served these with habanero raspberry jam, a traditional tzatziki, and a sour cream and garlic dip. A little tip: The mixture is a little sticky so make sure to have a nice little bowl of water to dip your fingers from time to time.
Thank you Linda T, you made my dish the talk of the party!

Move over IKEA, I don't need your meatballs anymore. I made these using gluten free bread crumbs. At first, the mixture is really wet, don't panic. Keep mixing and let it rest a minute or two. It will firm up. I have made four batches so far and love the outcome; tender to the tooth but robust enough to not fall apart at the touch of a fork or tongs when handling. I use half the salt written. These freeze well too. I served them with blueberry habanero jam and Sriracha/sour cream. All delicious! Thank you for the recipe.

I doubled the recipe (I cook for the week for my mom and I. ) I used Turkey instead of beef with the ground pork. I also used Stevia instead of sugar. The rest was the same. Oh, I put them in muffin tins in the oven at 425°f instead of stovetop frying. The result was super yummy! Less work too!
Great recipe and authentic to what my mother in law made except she added All Spice which was a required spice for these in Sweden.

Way too salty. I cut the salt to 1/2 tsp, and they were plenty salty. I also thought there was too much liquid for the volume of bread crumbs. I cut it to 1/2 cup total, and it was enough. Add about 1/4 tsp allspice for that authentic Swedish Meatball flavor.

Very, very good. Even my mother, who does not like meatballs, loved these.

I did use Italian season bread crumbs because that's all I had and added onion and garlic granules and a pinch of nutmeg. I also used about a pound and a half of ground/minced beef and ended up needing a bit more bread crumbs but it was also humid (I live in Texas and it was Spring). All-in-all, "Make Again."

Between three people, we had leftovers and I swear they taste even better the next day. You could even let the meat rest in the fridge to let the spices blend.

I suggest trying with lingonberry jam/sauce from Ikea (maybe even cloudberry?) and/or sour cream mix. The sour cream mix I made, I just used the last of some sour cream, added a health amount of dill, dash of salt, onion and garlic granules, and a small splash of lemon juice. Mix and try not to let the dog lick it when taking a picture. Silly girl.

I will absolutely be making this again.

Tack så mycket for such a great recipe.

I make it as the recipe dictates but with only half the salt. I have 3 kids aged 6 & under, who are fussy eaters & at any given meal only two will actually like what I put on the table. I make double portions, as it one of the few meals that EVERYONE in the family will eat. I have tried buying store bought but that gets rejected & I'm back to this "labor of love". A good substitute to lingonberry sauce (hard to find) is strawberry jam mixed with a little white vinegar & a pinch of salt

I'm being generous by giving this recipe 3 *s. I should have listened to my inner voice the first time, which told me to add a couple of finely minced garlic cloves when sautéing the onions. Also, several sprigs of minced flat leaf Italian parsley would add more flavor, as would a sprinkle of nutmeg. I made them once again (my way) and they were delicious.

My mama is from Sweden this recipe is almost identical but the one thing she never added is sugar. She always told me the secret ingredient was the white pepper . Also the original recipe has ground beef, ground pork and ground veal. Very good ! Must try if you haven't!!! My neighbor loves it so much she always asks for the leftover gravy for bread dipping !!!

Very good. Followed recipe exactly, but needed more breadcrumbs. I baked the meatballs in a 350 degree oven for 25 minutes instead of on the stove as I don't have a stove top pan big enough to hold 48 meatballs ;-) Next time I will use less salt.

Growing up, my Scots-Irish American family spent every Christmas Eve with a Swedish-French family who’d served a huge buffet after midnight church services (alternating between Lutheran & Catholic Churches.) The Swedish Meatballs and Baked Hams were the star buffet attractions! It just wouldn’t be Christmas without Swedish Meatballs and Baked Ham…but we enjoy the Swedish Meatballs all through the year, also. Great Recipe!
Loved this recipe for 70 years. My grandmother (Dane) had the same recipe! Sometimes meatballs sometimes meatloaf.

This is basically the same recipe my family has been using for generations. Ours uses 1/2 tsp less salt and no sugar. Served with lingonberry jam. Brown or creamy sauce/ gravy if serving as a main. Yum.

i have made this as written many times. My youngest son (age 55) wants it at least twice a month. I do make the brown gravy from another recipe sometimes and plan to try the sherry gravy from another recipe this time
Easy and simple! Taste delicious. My go to recipe from now on.
As a diabetic, I always get frustrated/irritated when I see sugar in a recipe. I simply omit sugar or substitute Splenda. I will be making these tonight and can't wait!
love it , i remember having in Norway all time and still have
Lacks: nutmeg, black pepper and soy sauce This is a very simplified recipe and not authentic. Good if you don't have any spices or soy sauce at home
